@l23r Yes and no. From what I understand, in council housing they will move you to accommodate the size of your family - within limitation. In the US, it's called section 8 housing, atleast in NY that's what it's called. You go on a list, and it's first come first serve. Depending on your income, where you are on the list etc. The program provides families with a certificate or voucher that allows them to lease an apartment or home they otherwise couldn’t afford.

Families pay some “reasonable rent,” which is a percentage of their income; the remaining rent is covered by the local housing authority. Total rents are determined by the local housing authority, and are capped by the Fair Market Rent (FMR), which is set by HUD (US Department of Housing and Urban Development). Alot of landlords will not rent to section 8 tenants, due to the fact that there is little recourse for damages. You can email your local section 8 office with documents and repair receipts, but they won't always pay. Alot of times if families have trashed the place, they lose their housing vouchers which means no more assistance. Doesn't really help the landlord recover costs though. And section eight (depending on your state) doesn't really care if you continue to breed. They won't stuff 5 people into a two bedroom if the fire code doesn't allow more than four, but that's about it.
